implementationPlan.description:
RE-ANCHOR AND CORRECT THE ROW'S STALE PREMISES. No edits in this step. The description and the rejection both describe a tree that no longer exists; record what is actually true before touching anything.

(a) Record `git rev-parse HEAD` (expect 3c054aed or later). The rejection anchors on delivery commit e1e35a6c — stale.

(b) ADOPT the two DONE dependencies from epicSiblings rather than re-measuring their work: task-9d4aab86 (DONE) and task-3aa6acdb (DONE, completion dd1c227d65f0). Read their completionSummary/reviewSummary.

(c) DISCHARGE DoD 4 BY ADOPTION, NOT BY EDITING. The QA rejection said 'let the child reach DONE, then resubmit with committed dependency evidence'. Verify and record: `wc -l apps/daemon/src/daemon-store-dependencies.ts` = 169 (<400, inside the <=250 extraction target); daemon-store-foundation-composition.ts exists; the composition behavior and export surface are unchanged (daemon-store-dependencies.ts still re-exports createStoreDependencies, StoreDependencyConfig and agentCapabilitiesFor at the old specifier). DO NOT EDIT EITHER STORE PATH — the rejection forbids it and composition.ts is currently DIRTY under the live sibling row task-ed89967f.

(d) RE-MEASURE THE CLAIMED FAILURES BEFORE FIXING ANYTHING. Run standalone and unpiped:
`pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run --root . --config package.json src/activation/activation-telemetry-launch.test.ts src/activation/activation-run-commit.test.ts src/work/launch-template-producer.test.ts`
ARCHITECT MEASURED: **Test Files 3 passed (3), Tests 131 passed (131)** — the 10 + 2 + 3 committed failures the description is premised on are ALREADY FIXED. If your run agrees, do NOT re-implement fixes for them; re-implementing a landed surface is a silent duplicate. If your run DISAGREES, that is the real work — record the exact failing arms and proceed red-first.

(e) Record `git status --porcelain` and line counts for the eight non-store owned paths (all measured clean: 143 / 845 / 249 / 619 / 196 / 1071 / 290 / 3486), plus the full-lane pre-diff baseline `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` with its count line and exact failing set. Read the OUTPUT, not the exit code — 'No test files found' and 'No projects matched the filters' both exit 0.

DoD 1 — THE VERIFY-OR-BLOCK SEALED-FIELD TRACE. This is the row's real intellectual deliverable. Produce a written trace, not an impression.

Trace `renderedContext` bytes and `contextManifestDigest` from the launch-template authority through EVERY runner request and the durable replay digest. Read these (do not edit the unowned ones): work/launch-template-producer.ts, work/foundation-attempt-contracts.ts (OWNED), work/foundation-attempt-service.ts, work/foundation-attempt-codec.ts, work/foundation-attempt-store.ts, work/foundation-context-prelaunch.ts.

SETTLE THIS SPECIFIC QUESTION, because a prior architect filed it as a defect and I could not confirm it. The ordering claim is TRUE: foundation-attempt-service.ts:107 computes `identity = identifyFoundationDispatch(request, sealed.manifest)`, :112 and :140 compare it for replay conflict, :133 commits it as requestDigest — all BEFORE :180 seals the context. So the replay digest provably does not contain the two sealed fields.
THE OPEN QUESTION IS WHETHER THAT IS A DEFECT. My reading says no: foundation-attempt-codec.ts:197-204 digests {activationRequestDigest, binding, graphSnapshot, inputManifest} — all caller-supplied — while sealFoundationContext's inputs are either covered by that digest (nodeKey, sessionId via binding; projectId via the activation bytes) or server-minted (attemptRef from the durable activation record; decidedAt from the activation decision). If so, a caller cannot vary the sealed context independently of digested material and the exclusion is sound, as the production comment at :171-179 argues.
CONFIRM OR REFUTE IT YOURSELF. For each of the five seal inputs, name where it comes from and whether a caller can influence it without changing a digested byte.

OUTCOME A — no caller must synthesize or omit either field: record the trace as durable evidence (a row comment, since it will exceed the completionSummary cap) and continue. DoD 1 is then met by verification.
OUTCOME B — some caller must synthesize or omit one: STOP and moe.report_blocked. Name the exact caller, the field, and the unowned production file that would have to change. DoD 1 says report blocked 'rather than weakening the launcher parser', and rail 1 says request an amendment or split before expanding. Do NOT edit foundation-attempt-service.ts (unowned, 247 lines) and do NOT loosen the parser to make a caller fit.

DoD 2 — PROVE THE FIXTURES ARE TRUTHFUL, NOT MERELY GREEN. Edit only the three owned test files.

The suite passes 131/131, which is NOT evidence for this DoD: a green suite can pin obsolete behavior. Verify each claim and add the missing assertion where a check is absent or weak.

(a) LIVE SCHEMA. Confirm the telemetry and launch-template fixtures build requests from the EXACT live request schema — the same shape production constructs, not a hand-rolled literal that has drifted. Where a fixture hand-builds a request, assert its key set against the production type/constant rather than a copied literal. A fixture that reimplements the shape cannot detect a shape change.

(b) TRUTHFUL DISTINCTIONS. REFUSED, NOT_ATTEMPTED and UNKNOWN must remain distinguishable and correctly assigned, and launcher-owned reason/layer must stay attributed to the launcher rather than restamped by the daemon. For every arm asserting one of these outcomes, assert the EXACT stable reason code AND the refusing layer — never merely that the operation did not succeed. Where more than one layer can refuse, assert which one did.

(c) NON-VACUITY CHECK, applied honestly: for each assertion you rely on, ask whether a SINGLE edit could move both the expected and the actual side (for example an expected constant imported from the module under test). If so, pin the expectation independently.

Run the three focused files and require them green with a nonzero count.

DoD 3 — PROVE REPLAY IDEMPOTENCY BY MUTATION. This step is load-bearing: it is what converts a green suite into evidence.

(a) POSITIVE: same key, same admitted bytes replays idempotently — the second dispatch adopts the durable outcome and does NOT launch again. foundation-attempt-service.ts:145-149 is the adoption path ('Replay adopts durable output or remains in flight; it never launches again'). Assert no second launch effect, not merely a successful return.

(b) NEGATIVE: any changed admitted byte refuses at the EXACT replay-conflict code and layer, BEFORE effects. The production comparisons are :112 (pre-reservation) and :140 (post-commit race), both refusing FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_REPLAY_MISMATCH. Assert that exact code and its layer, and assert no effect was committed.

(c) MUTATION DRILLS, each reddening its OWN named arm, one degree at a time. Capture exact-path `git status --porcelain` first; all owned files are TRACKED and CLEAN, so `git diff --exit-code` plus SHA equality is a valid restore proof.
  1. Change one admitted byte in the request and confirm the mismatch arm reds if the guard is loosened — i.e. mutate the :112 comparison to always pass and require the negative arm to red. If it stays GREEN, the arm is vacuous: that is a FINDING, and the fix is to add the assertion that would have caught it.
  2. Mutate the :140 post-commit comparison the same way and require its arm to red.
  3. Mutate the adoption branch at :145-149 to re-launch and require the idempotency arm to red.
Restore each separately and prove the restore before the next.

MUTATE ONLY OWNED FILES. If a drill would require mutating foundation-attempt-service.ts (UNOWNED), do not do it — record which property is therefore unproven from inside this row's ownership, and say so plainly in the completion record rather than claiming coverage you could not obtain.

DoD 5 — FINAL VERIFICATION, ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, AND LANDING.

(a) Load `adversarial-self-review` and read the diff as an attacker: twice-and-concurrent dispatch of the same key; a request whose only change is a sealed field; an empty or absent manifest; a launcher that returns a refusal shape the daemon might restamp; UTF-8 edge bytes through the fatal decoder at foundation-attempt-contracts.ts:231-238; and whether any arm you added would still pass against an empty result.

(b) Run the three focused owned files, then `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck`, then the FULL `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`. Require nonzero `Test Files`/`Tests` count lines on every leg and typecheck exit 0 with its `$ tsc` echo. Per DoD 5, the full daemon lane must be green EXCEPT separately-owned broker/HTTP prerequisites — attribute any failure by merge-base-versus-HEAD delta and disclose foreign red VERBATIM with exact failing lines and paths. Note that apps/daemon/src/http/ currently holds several foreign dirty and untracked http-listener* modules from live sibling rows; red there is foreign.

(c) Confirm the delta intersected with this row's owned paths is EMPTY, and that the two store paths were never edited by you (`git diff` on daemon-store-dependencies.ts must be empty; daemon-store-foundation-composition.ts stays dirty exactly as task-ed89967f left it — do not revert, stage or clean it).

(d) LANDING. Report every touched path in complete_step.modifiedFiles and declare the owned paths with moe.declare_files — post-flight lands by measured attribution, so an undeclared path is not swept. Do NOT hand-commit; a manual `git commit` fires no post-flight hook and leaves task.commits empty, which is half of why this row was rejected. Do not verify your own landing before exit.

(e) In completionSummary state plainly what this row actually did versus what its description claimed: that the 15 committed failures were already fixed at claim time (131/131 green, measured), that DoD 4 was discharged by adopting child task-3aa6acdb's landing (169 lines) rather than by editing delegated store paths, the DoD 1 trace outcome, and which properties the drills proved. Put the full trace, drill sheet with red lines and mutant SHAs, and the foreign-red disclosure into row comments — each under ~4500 chars, since comments truncate SILENTLY at 5000.

MEASURED 2026-09-02 at HEAD 3c054aed. THE ROW'S DESCRIPTION IS STALE IN BOTH DIRECTIONS — re-measure before believing any of it.

### 1. THE 15 COMMITTED FAILURES ARE ALREADY FIXED
The description opens 'Acceptance follow-up for 10 activation-telemetry, 2 activation-run-commit, and 3 launch-template-producer committed failures'. I ran all three focused files:
`pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run --root . --config package.json src/activation/activation-telemetry-launch.test.ts src/activation/activation-run-commit.test.ts src/work/launch-template-producer.test.ts`

### 2. DoD 4 IS SATISFIED BY THE CHILD, NOT BY THIS ROW
The QA rejection was solely: 'At delivery commit e1e35a6c this file is exactly 490 physical lines and daemon-store-foundation-composition.ts/.js are absent. Child task-3aa6acdb is WORKING, unmerged... let the child reach DONE, then resubmit with committed dependency evidence.'
Measured now: task-3aa6acdb is DONE (completion dd1c227d65f0). apps/daemon/src/daemon-store-dependencies.ts is **169 lines** (<400, and inside the '<=250 extraction' target). daemon-store-foundation-composition.ts exists. Both dependsOn rows (task-9d4aab86, task-3aa6acdb) are DONE. So DoD 4 is discharged by ADOPTION + verification, exactly as the rejection instructed.
DO NOT EDIT THE TWO STORE PATHS. The rejection says 'Do not edit delegated store paths here', and composition.ts is CURRENTLY DIRTY under task-ed89967f, which is actively adding a one-line principalId forward. Touching it collides with a live row.

### 3. THE CLAIMED PRE-SEAL IDENTITY DEFECT DOES NOT SURVIVE MEASUREMENT
A prior architect (msg from architect-5e59a71e) asserted the real DoD-1/3 gap is in OMITTED production apps/daemon/src/work/foundation-attempt-service.ts, which 'commits pre-seal identity.bytes, so durable replay excludes both sealed fields'. I traced it. The ORDERING claim is TRUE but the DEFECT conclusion is NOT established:
- foundation-attempt-service.ts:107 `identity = identifyFoundationDispatch(request, sealed.manifest)`; :112 and :140 are the replay-conflict comparisons; :133 commits `requestDigest: identity.digest`.
- :180 `deps.context.sealFoundationContext({attemptRef, nodeKey, projectId, sessionId}, activation.decision.decidedAt)` runs strictly AFTER. So the durable replay digest indeed does not contain renderedContext/contextManifestDigest.
- BUT foundation-attempt-codec.ts:197-204 shows identifyFoundationDispatch digests {activationRequestDigest: sha256Hex(request.activationRequestBytes), binding, graphSnapshot, inputManifest} — i.e. ALL CALLER-SUPPLIED material — while the seal's five inputs are either already covered by that digest (nodeKey and sessionId via binding, projectId via the activation bytes) or SERVER-MINTED (attemptRef from the durable activation record, decidedAt from the activation decision).
- A caller therefore cannot vary the sealed context independently of digested material, which is precisely what the production comment at :171-179 argues ('Nothing about argv, a ref or a re-render reaches the seal').
CONCLUSION: on current evidence DoD 1's verify-or-block trace should PASS with no caller needing to synthesize or omit either field, and no production change is warranted. That is why this plan contains NO implementation step and does NOT request foundation-attempt-service.ts (247 lines, currently UNOWNED). Step 2 makes the worker complete the trace rigorously rather than adopt my partial one.

planningNotes.risks:
THE BIGGEST RISK IS INVENTING WORK. Two of this row's three stated premises are already closed (15 failures fixed; store extraction landed). A worker who takes the description at face value will re-implement landed work and collide with its owner. Every step below re-measures before acting.
THE SECOND BIGGEST RISK IS CLOSING VACUOUSLY. 131 green tests are not evidence for DoD 2 or DoD 3. A suite can be green because it pins obsolete behavior — which is exactly what the prior architect alleged about foundation-attempt-service.test.ts. The step-4 drills are the load-bearing part of this row: if a mutation does not redden a named arm, that is a FINDING and the fix is to add the missing assertion, not to record a pass.
IF THE TRACE CONTRADICTS ME, BLOCK — DO NOT WIDEN. DoD 1 is explicitly verify-or-block. If step 2 finds a caller that must synthesize or omit renderedContext/contextManifestDigest, the required output is moe.report_blocked naming that caller and the unowned production file, NOT an edit to foundation-attempt-service.ts (unowned, 247 lines) and NOT a weakened launcher parser. Rail 1: request an amendment or split before expanding.
DO NOT TOUCH THE STORE PATHS. daemon-store-foundation-composition.ts is dirty RIGHT NOW under task-ed89967f (a live sibling adding a one-line principalId forward). Editing, reverting or staging it destroys another row's in-flight work.
DELIVERY: the prior attempt was rejected partly for evidence, and the row's own history shows a delivery commit (e1e35a6c) that could not satisfy DoD 4. Declare owned paths and exit through the wrapper; a manual commit fires no post-flight hook.
CROSS-PLATFORM: launch-template-producer and the context seal handle rendered bytes and UTF-8 decoding (foundation-attempt-contracts.ts:231-238 decodes with fatal:true). Any fixture that hard-codes a newline convention will behave differently on Windows; assert on bytes, not on formatted text.
SHARED CHECKOUT: ~60 foreign dirty paths. Never revert, stash, `git add -A`, `git clean -fd` or `git checkout -- .`.
